subject: Differences in shiny plots on local machine and web server

messages.author: 5d5a6103d3120fa5
messages.subject: Differences in shiny plots on local machine and web server
parts:
I am having trouble getting the plots in my shiny app on a web server to look the same as those produced locally on my machine.

This the address of the shiny app on the web (takes a couple of seconds to load):
http://witt.null2.net/shiny/wicpyr/

I have put the code into my first GitHub, so hopefully others can see a reproduced example of the plots on their local machine...
shiny::runGitHub('wicpyr', 'gjabel')

There are some small differences in the font size, plot border size, and in the version on the web server some of the underlying coloured bars (they are overlayed in the R plotting function) are slightly visible at the end of some bars.

After reading around I thought the differences might be solved or caused by the Cairo package. I have add
options(shiny.usecairo = FALSE)
or
options(shiny.usecairo = TRUE)
to both the ui.R and server.R (I wasn't definite as to the correct place) but neither combination did anything to alter the appearance of the plots on the web server.

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Differences in shiny plots on local machine and web server
parts:
What platform are you using locally? There are some inherent differences in R's font rendering in Linux vs. Windows vs. Mac. As for the bar ends, it might be caused by antialiasing in Linux. If you're running Windows locally, it will align graphical objects to pixel boundaries, which might avoid this issue. You might be able to get that to look similar by passing antialias="none" to renderPlot().

-Winston

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Differences in shiny plots on local machine and web server
parts:
I don't think it's possible to get fonts looking exactly the same between Windows and Linux. What you could do, though, is change the font size with the cex argument, if you're using base graphics. See ?par for more information on that topic.

-Winston
